response:
It's clear you love your daughter and pay close attention to her wellbeing. What you're describing—intense crying and "freaking out" over small things—can be a sign that stress is building up beyond what she can manage on her own, and it's worth taking seriously. Perfectionism and academic pressure often show up this way in bright, high-achieving kids.

Reaching out for support isn't an overreaction. You might start with her pediatrician, who can rule out other factors and refer you to a counselor or therapist experienced with children and anxiety. In the meantime, gentle conversations where you let her know her worth isn't tied to grades can help take some pressure off. If she ever mentions wanting to hurt herself or expresses hopelessness, treat that as urgent and seek help right away.

Trust your instinct that something feels off—you clearly know her well, and getting her support now can make a real difference.
